hypotheses.reasoning: audit-consumer (v3.23.3) crashes with a RangeError (maximum call stack size exceeded) in expandReferences while processing msg-982640 at offset 620792. On every restart it resumes at the same committed offset 620792 because the offset was never advanced past the bad message, so it crashes again in a loop (restarts 1-3, with growing backoff). The message is malformed or deeply nested and repeatedly jams the consumer, which explains the CrashLoopBackOff and the rising audit.events lag. Upstream services (account-svc, auth-svc, edge-proxy, session-cache, accounts-db) show no errors, so they are not the origin. accounts-db vacuum and checkpoint lines are routine and unrelated.

A stack overflow could in principle come from recursion depth, but the trigger is one specific message that fails identically on every retry, and no memory or pool pressure appears in the logs. Less likely than a poison message.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or quarantine msg-982640 (offset 620792) from audit.events, moving it to a dead-letter topic, so the consumer can advance past the offset. Then resume the consumer and let it drain the lag. Add a guard in expandReferences against deep or cyclic references, and make the consumer dead-letter messages that throw instead of crashing the process on each restart.
